author: A Robot
objectives: Students will identify and name the four chambers of the heart, the four heart valves, and the major vessels entering and leaving the heart.
Students will trace the path of blood through the heart's dual circulation, naming each chamber, valve, and vessel in order.
Students will distinguish the pulmonary circuit from the systemic circuit and explain why the right and left sides of the heart serve different circulatory functions.

Students will explain why the left ventricle has a substantially thicker myocardium than the right ventricle, relating wall thickness to the pressure required to perfuse the systemic versus pulmonary circuits.
Students will describe the function of the atrioventricular and semilunar valves in preventing backflow, and identify which valves separate which chambers or chamber-vessel pairs.

modules.description: An introduction to the basic structure of the human heart, including its chambers and major vessels.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Identify the four chambers of the heart: right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle.
Identify the major vessels connected to the heart: superior/inferior vena cava, pulmonary arteries/veins, and aorta.
instructions: Identify the four chambers as they are highlighted.

clips.changeMeaning: The heart model is introduced, providing a central view of the organ.
clips.narration: This is a model of the human heart, a vital organ responsible for pumping blood throughout the body. Let's explore its main structures.

clips.changeMeaning: Labels and highlight for the four chambers of the heart are added.
clips.narration: The heart has four chambers: the right atrium, the right ventricle, the left atrium, and the left ventricle. These chambers work together to pump blood.

modules.description: Tracing the path of blood through the heart's pulmonary and systemic circuits.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Trace the path of blood through the heart, naming each chamber, valve, and vessel in order.
Distinguish the pulmonary circuit from the systemic circuit.
Explain the different functions of the right and left sides of the heart.
instructions: Observe the heart model and valves.
Follow the highlighted paths to understand blood flow.
Note the different colors representing deoxygenated (red) and oxygenated (blue) blood.

clips.changeMeaning: The four valves of the heart are introduced and labeled.
clips.narration: Four valves ensure blood flows in the correct direction: the tricuspid valve between the right atrium and ventricle, the pulmonary valve at the exit of the right ventricle, the mitral valve between the left atrium and ventricle, and the aortic valve at the exit of the left ventricle.

clips.changeMeaning: The path of deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary circuit is visualized.
clips.narration: Deoxygenated blood from the body enters the right atrium, passes through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, and is pumped through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary artery, heading to the lungs. This is the pulmonary circuit.

clips.changeMeaning: The path of oxygenated blood through the systemic circuit is visualized.
clips.narration: Oxygenated blood returns from the lungs via the pulmonary veins to the left atrium, passes through the mitral valve into the left ventricle, and is pumped through the aortic valve and aorta to the rest of the body. This is the systemic circuit.

modules.description: Explaining the difference in myocardial thickness between ventricles and the role of valves.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Explain why the left ventricle is thicker than the right ventricle.
Describe how valves prevent backflow during the cardiac cycle.
instructions: Observe the difference in ventricular wall thickness.
Visualize the one-way action of the heart valves.

clips.changeMeaning: The difference in wall thickness between the left and right ventricles is highlighted.
clips.narration: Notice the significantly thicker wall of the left ventricle compared to the right. This is because the left ventricle must generate much higher pressure to pump blood to the entire body, while the right ventricle only needs to pump blood to the nearby lungs.

clips.changeMeaning: An animation demonstrating valve function to prevent backflow is shown.
clips.narration: The heart valves act like one-way doors, opening to allow blood flow forward and snapping shut to prevent any backflow during the cardiac cycle, ensuring efficient pumping.
